title: Separating one AI brain from multiple execution surfaces
goal: Test a workflow that reserves stateful coding execution for work that needs local state.
context: ChatGPT Chat, plugins, Codex, and API runtimes can overlap, but they have different state and latency boundaries.
problem: The previous workflow did not distinguish product reasoning and online actions from work that required a local repository.
actions: Defined five task surfaces: Chat, Plugin, Codex, Runtime, and Human.
Added human gates for risky, public, and irreversible actions.

decisions.decision: Use one strong reasoning core before adding specialist agents.
decisions.reason: Multiple weak agents often repeat context and require another synthesis step.
alternatives_considered: Run six or seven agents on every task.
Use Codex as the default entry point for all technical work.

trade_offs: The routing policy must be maintained as new plugins and execution surfaces appear.
Some local implementation reasoning remains inside Codex.
result: Representative tasks can be routed to the minimum required surface with explicit secondary roles and approval gates.
lessons: Multi-agent orchestration is valuable when roles have different tools or boundaries, not merely different personalities.
Contracts and evidence are more reliable than transferring long chat histories.
evidence: The routing test suite covers Chat, Plugin, Codex, Runtime, and Human-gate paths.
The Execution Packet generator produces a bounded local implementation contract.
audience: AI engineers, solo founders, developer-tool builders, and technical recruiters
